property_summary: For any caller, newEmergencyOracle either succeeds and emits NewEmergencyOracle (reference) or reverts (mutant); the reference must succeed when msg.sender equals jojoTeam, while the mutant always reverts.
For any valid string description and when msg.sender equals jojoTeam, calling newEmergencyOracle on the reference contract always succeeds, while the mutant always reverts.
A call to newEmergencyOracle by the authorized jojoTeam must succeed (not revert); the mutant always reverts because the onlyJojoTeam modifier unconditionally reverts regardless of caller.
When the caller is the jojoTeam, newEmergencyOracle must not revert; the mutant always reverts due to the unconditional revert replacing the require.

For any caller, newEmergencyOracle succeeds (does not revert) if and only if msg.sender equals the jojoTeam address. The mutant breaks this by requiring msg.sender == address(0) instead, so the real team can never create an oracle, while address(0) (which cannot be a caller) becomes the only allowed sender.

For any caller, a call to newEmergencyOracle will succeed (not revert) if and only if the caller is address(jojoTeam), which is initially address(0); the buggy version instead reverts for all real callers because it requires msg.sender == address(0), which is impossible for an EOA or contract.

The mutant breaks this by requiring msg.sender == address(0) instead, so the real team can never create an oracle, while address(0) (which cannot be a caller) becomes the only allowed sender.

For any initial jojoTeam address set by the contract, a call to newEmergencyOracle by that address always succeeds and emits NewEmergencyOracle, while the buggy version always reverts for that same address, preventing oracle creation.
Only the jojoTeam address can successfully create a new emergency oracle.

The owner of the newly created EmergencyOracle must be msg.sender; the mutant passes a constant address, so the owner is not the caller, breaking the invariant.
After calling newEmergencyOracle, the owner of the newly created EmergencyOracle contract must be msg.sender; the mutant sets it to a constant address, violating this rule.
After calling newEmergencyOracle, the returned EmergencyOracle owner must be the caller (msg.sender); the mutant sets the owner to a fixed address, violating this rule.
After any caller invokes newEmergencyOracle, the owner of the newly created EmergencyOracle contract must be msg.sender; the mutant passes a constant address, breaking this invariant.
After any successful `newEmergencyOracle` call, the reference contract always emits a `NewEmergencyOracle` event, whereas the buggy version never emits this event, breaking external observability.

After a successful newEmergencyOracle call, the contract's code must contain a NewEmergencyOracle event emission; the bug deletes it, so a successful call yields exactly zero event logs in the buggy version while the reference yields at least one.

After a successful newEmergencyOracle call, the total number of NewEmergencyOracle events emitted (as counted by a getter in a minimal recorder) must be strictly greater than before; the bug deletes the emit so the count stays unchanged.

For any successful call to newEmergencyOracle, the reference contract emits exactly one NewEmergencyOracle event, while the buggy version emits none, which can be detected by observing that the number of events logged in the transaction increases by one in the reference but zero in the mutant.

The event emitted by newEmergencyOracle always records the immediate msg.sender (the original owner) in the reference, but the mutant incorrectly emits tx.origin, so whenever a contract calls newEmergencyOracle on behalf of the JOJO team the emitted owner differs.
